ops.oldText: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable upon its creation. Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3, and the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies to any Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

input.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we commission, so we have reversed the assignment in 14.2 and confirmed Vendor keeps its pre-existing Vendor Technology with the Section 13.2 perpetual licence to anything embedded in a Deliverable. A revocable, term-limited licence to Deliverables we pay for is not workable for us; if Vendor cannot assign, our fallback is Vendor ownership with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence for us to use, modify, and sublicense the Deliverables for our business.
input.summary: Reverse Deliverable ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; preserve Vendor Technology retention and embedded-IP licence.
